headlines.summary_en: Jin10 Data, August 31 - This morning, the three major indices opened lower, rebounded, then pulled back at the close. The AI corpus sector rose steadily, with Mango Excellent Media and Rongxin Culture both hitting 20cm limit-up, and Zhongguang Tianze and Shanghai Film among multiple limit-ups. The coal mining sector lifted intraday, with Zhengzhou Coal Power hitting limit-up and Dayou Energy up over 6%. Real estate services were active, with Tefa Service up over 10%. Liquid-cooled server stocks strengthened, with Jinfu Technology, Jindi Shares and Kangsheng Shares among multiple limit-ups. Additionally, consumer electronics, sports, kitchen and bathroom appliances, banks and PCB sectors led gains. The real estate development sector opened high and fell, with Xiangjiang Holding and Yingxin Development down over 5%. headlines.title_en: Vice President of the China Federation of Logistics and Purchasing: August manufacturing PMI was affected by extreme weather such as high temperatures, typhoons, and torrential rain and flooding.
headlines.summary_en: He Hui, Vice President of the China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing, said that in August, both domestic and foreign market demand in manufacturing expanded. The new orders index and new export orders index both rose notably year-on-year and month-on-month, and the month-on-month change in market demand was better than the same period last year, indicating that stronger policy support has effectively boosted economic development momentum.

headlines.title_en: The global trade and economic friction index remained at a high level in June, with the electronics industry ranking first.
headlines.summary_en: This morning, the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT) held a press conference releasing the latest global economic and trade friction data, showing the June global economic and trade friction index remained high. On the composite index, the June 2026 global economic and trade friction index was 102, a high level. The amount involved in global economic and trade friction measures rose 2.4% year-on-year and 11.8% month-on-month. By country index, among the 20 countries (regions) monitored, India, the U.S. and the EU ranked top three. CCPIT spokesperson Yang Fan said the U.S. continues to intensify use of unilateral sanctions, export controls, Section 232 tariffs, Section 301 investigations and other trade protection tools, keeping its global trade friction amount ranked first for seven consecutive months. headlines.title_en: Wall Street Breakfast | August 31, 2026
headlines.summary_en: U.S. stocks fell last Friday, the 2-year Treasury yield rose more than 10 basis points, and gold slumped 3%. Over the weekend, the U.S. and Iran traded strikes, and international crude oil rose over 2% in early Asian trading Monday. U.S. officials said Sunday U.S. forces struck two weapons sites on Iran's Larak Island and accused Iran of trying to lay mines in the Strait; Iran's military said it fired missiles at a U.S. base. Fed Chair Warsh delivered a hawkish Jackson Hole debut, the most hawkish Jackson Hole speech since 2009, hinting at rate hikes if inflation does not fall quickly. Market odds for a September hike rose from 35% to nearly 60%, with possibly two hikes before March 2027. U.S. nonfarm payrolls were preliminarily revised down by 79,000, opposite to market expectations of an upward revision of 183,000, as the labor market cooling continues. During Jackson Hole, ECB officials warned on inflation and leaned toward a September hike, while the BoE governor signaled no rush. Reports said the U.S. bought yen with euro sales ahead of...
